# HamariHawa (ہماری ہوا · हमारी हवा, "our air")

> A free, non-commercial public-awareness site that shows, live, what satellites see in the air over Pakistan and India (all of both countries; the Indus-Gangetic Plain, 25–35.5°N, 66–88.5°E, until 17 October 2026): fires, smoke, nitrogen dioxide from traffic and industry, known pollution sources, and what the air means for health in 58 cities. In English, Urdu and Hindi.

## Pages
- [Live map](https://hamarihawa.org/): fire detections from the last 24 h / 48 h / 7 days, each named after the nearest village and tagged when it sits on a known brick kiln, landfill, industrial estate or always-hot site; satellite layers (14-day traffic & industry NO₂, haze/AOD, smoke index, true colour); live AQI and health estimates for 58 cities (the list is at https://hamarihawa.org/air/); source shares from published studies; what can be done about transport.
- [Pollution sites](https://hamarihawa.org/sites/): traffic NO₂ hotspots, landfills with methane plumes, power and industrial plants with CO₂ plumes, always-hot industrial sites and the districts with the most brick kilns.
- [About, method and disclaimer](https://hamarihawa.org/about/): methods, limits, privacy, credits.
- [Use the data](https://hamarihawa.org/data/): Google Earth KML feed, how to use it in GIS tools, why Google Maps can't show live layers, JSON feeds and licences.
- [Two Punjabs: seven seasons of crop fires](https://hamarihawa.org/report/two-punjabs/): report. Fire spots seen by NASA's Suomi NPP (1 Oct-30 Nov) fell 95% in Indian Punjab from 2021 (70,527) to 2025 (3,714) but not in Pakistani Punjab (9,296 in 2019, 12,364 in 2025), which has had more since 2024 (3.3x in 2025). Corrected on 23 October 2026: fires on the Indian side of the border near Firozpur had been counted in Pakistani Punjab. Our Indian counts track India's official counts with correlation 0.99. Counts are a floor: much Indian burning has moved to after the 1:30 pm pass; we see no such shift in Pakistani Punjab. Data: https://hamarihawa.org/report/two-punjabs/seasons.json
- [Madhya Pradesh overtakes Indian Punjab: satellite fire spots in October, 2019–2026](https://hamarihawa.org/report/madhya-pradesh-indian-punjab-fire-spots/): report. From 1 to 24 October 2026 Madhya Pradesh had its most satellite fire spots in eight years, and Indian Punjab and Haryana their fewest. Every number is in https://hamarihawa.org/report/madhya-pradesh-indian-punjab-fire-spots/data.json with the evidence record it came from.
- [Reports](https://hamarihawa.org/reports/): list of HamariHawa reports.
- [Fire trends](https://hamarihawa.org/trends/): every October–November burning season since 2019 compared (Suomi NPP counts, so years compare fairly), this season against the same dates last year, season totals, the share of fires seen on the night pass, and a day-by-day district bubble map.
- [City air](https://hamarihawa.org/air/): one page per city for 58 cities in Pakistan and India (https://hamarihawa.org/air/lahore/, /air/delhi/ …): which way the wind is blowing now, the fires within 250 km upwind in the last 24 hours by district and direction, the week's fires within 250 km, a close-up map of the last 24 hours' fires, the fires within 50 and 250 km on each of the last 30 days, this crop-burning season against every season since 2019 (Suomi NPP counts), the city's approximate 14-day NO₂ and its trend, the landfills with measured methane plumes (Carbon Mapper, kg/h, ranked among the measured landfill records in Pakistan and India), the plants, industrial areas, always-hot sites and brick kilns within 50 km, how the city ranks among the 58 on each measure, and the current AQI (Copernicus CAMS model estimates). These are measurements around a city, not shares of what is in its air. Updated every 15 minutes. Every number is also at https://hamarihawa.org/api/city?id=lahore (JSON; ids as in the page URLs).
- [City rankings](https://hamarihawa.org/rankings/): the 58 cities ranked by fire spots upwind right now, fire spots within 250 km (24 hours and 7 days), satellite NO₂ (14 days), landfill methane and brick kilns within 50 km. The fire tables change with each satellite pass.
- [Fires near me](https://hamarihawa.org/near-me/): is there a fire near you? The nearest fire NASA's satellites saw in the last 24 hours, its distance and direction, and counts within 25, 50 and 100 km, worked out in the visitor's browser from their approximate location, with a close-up map. Also lists the cities with the most fires within 250 km right now.
- [Daily fires](https://hamarihawa.org/fires/): one page per day (https://hamarihawa.org/fires/YYYY-MM-DD/, Pakistan time) with that day's fire spots in Pakistan and India, change on the day before, night share, busiest districts and villages, the same date in every year since 2019 (Suomi NPP counts), and a map. Every day since 1 October 2026 and every 1 Oct-30 Nov since 2019.
- [Fires by district](https://hamarihawa.org/district/): one page per district with frequent fires (https://hamarihawa.org/district/okara/, /district/sangrur/ …): this season against the same dates last year and every season since 2019, Suomi NPP only so years compare fairly.
- [What's new](https://hamarihawa.org/updates/): dated list of additions and fixes, newest first. Atom feed: https://hamarihawa.org/updates/feed.xml
- [24-month Lahore and Islamabad air report](https://hamarihawa.org/report/).

## Google Earth, Google Maps and GIS
- One link opens the whole live map in Google Earth: https://hamarihawa.org/hamarihawa.kml (a KML of network links). Layers: fires in the last 24 h (refreshed every 15 min) and 7 days; US AQI and PM2.5 now in 17 cities (Copernicus CAMS model, every 30 min); 2-week Sentinel-5P traffic and industry NO₂ with labelled hotspots (daily); NASA GIBS haze/aerosol and VIIRS true-colour photo (daily, one day behind); pollution sites (landfills, plants with CO₂ plumes, fossil power plants, always-hot industrial sites, brick-kiln belts).
- Google Earth Pro: Add → Network Link with that URL; layers refresh on their own. Google Earth web/mobile: download and import the file; it loads the latest data when opened.
- Google Maps does not accept live third-party layers. Google My Maps imports KML as a static copy with a 2,000-place limit per layer, so it suits the pollution-sites layer (https://hamarihawa.org/kml/sources.kml) but not the live fires.
- Individual KML layers for QGIS, ArcGIS, Civil 3D or any KML reader: https://hamarihawa.org/fires.kml?hours=24 (also 48, 168), https://hamarihawa.org/kml/air.kml, https://hamarihawa.org/kml/traffic.kml, https://hamarihawa.org/kml/satellite.kml, https://hamarihawa.org/kml/sources.kml

## Open data (JSON). Fire feed, fire archive and NO₂: CC BY 4.0 (except the fire type value "kiln", which comes from SentinelKilnDB and is CC BY-NC 4.0). Pollution sites and kiln layers: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, because they include SentinelKilnDB). Landfills, industrial areas, power plants and roads: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/fires?hours=24&v=2 (also 48, 168): fire feed with stats, events and points: names once in dict, points and events as rows described by fields and event_fields, times in minutes after t0, and the 7-day feed's distinct spots in spots. Requests without &v=2 (the v1 feed, retired 25 Oct 2026) get HTTP 410. trend.cur and trend.prev are the counts in the last window and the window before it, both cut from the same points and ending at the newest detection, so they compare like with like; trend.days the last 14 daily totals.
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/days: daily fire totals (days on Pakistan time, UTC+5; distinct spots; pk, in, night, crop, frp; snpp = spots Suomi NPP saw alone, comparable across years; sn splits it [all, PK, IN, night all, night PK, night IN]). Days carrying snc cover all of Pakistan and India; snc is the same split inside 25–35.5°N, 66–88.5°E (the area covered before October 2026), and a day without snc covers only that box. The whole archive was rebuilt for the whole region on 24–25 October 2026. Past seasons (1 Oct–30 Nov, 2019–2025) come from FIRMS final processing. Suomi NPP returned no data on 4–6 Nov 2024 (NASA outage) and missed its day pass on 31 Oct 2019, 2 Nov 2023, 3 Nov 2024 and 12 Nov 2025, so its counts on those days are missing, not zero; the all-satellite spots are unaffected. https://hamarihawa.org/api/day?d=YYYY-MM-DD gives that day's spots.
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/no2.json: 14-day NO₂ average metadata and labelled hotspots. Image: /api/no2.png (Web Mercator) or /api/no2-geo.png (equirectangular).
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/city?id=<id>: one city's numbers (ids as in /air/<id>/): fire spots now and upwind with the wind, fire spots within 50 and 250 km on each of the last 30 days (all satellites) and each season since 2019 from 1 October to the same date (Suomi NPP; gap days listed and left out), approximate 14-day NO₂ within 15 km with its ratio to the surrounding level and rank, and the measured and mapped sources within 50 km with ranks among the 58 cities. Fire counts are distinct spots: one fire seen by several satellites counts once a day. Live AQI is not included.
- https://hamarihawa.org/sources/sites.json: persistent pollution sites by category.
- https://hamarihawa.org/sources/kilns.json, osm-landfill.json, osm-industrial.json, plants.json, hotspots.json, carbonmapper.json, roads.json (major roads, context under the NO₂ layer): source layers.

## Key facts and methods
- Fires: NASA FIRMS near-real-time VIIRS 375 m (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and MODIS 1 km (Aqua, Terra). Satellites pass about 01:30 and 13:30 local time; data arrive about 3 hours later. Cloud cover at the last pass is drawn on the map, because fires under cloud can't be seen.
- Desert false alarms: over the Thar desert (25-29N, 70-74E) a single afternoon satellite pass sometimes flags hundreds of "fires" on hot sand that the other VIIRS satellites, passing within the hour, don't see. Such unconfirmed bursts are dropped from the feed and the archive.
- Fire type: tagged as brick kiln, landfill, industrial or always-hot site when within reach of a known source, or "near a town" near big towns; otherwise from ESA WorldCover 2021 land cover under the fire: "likely crop burning" (mostly cropland), "likely forest fire" (mostly forest; "forest or shifting cultivation" in North-East India), "open land" (scrub, grass, bare) or "mixed land". Fires outside Pakistan and India (by geoBoundaries country outlines) are left out. Earlier versions used the month instead of land cover ("likely crop burning" in Oct–Nov and Apr–May) and kept fires in Nepal and Bangladesh labelled as India. These are best guesses, not findings.
- Traffic NO₂: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric NO₂ from NASA GIBS, 14-day average over all of Pakistan and India; ratios are against the usual level around each place (the median over land in 5° blocks, smoothed), so southern cities are not judged against the northern plains. In big-city cores NO₂ is mostly from vehicle engines. Pixels are about 5 km wide, so the layer shows a city's traffic as one hotspot and corridors such as the GT Road belt, not individual roads; major roads from OpenStreetMap are drawn underneath for context.
- Wind: 10 m wind from the Open-Meteo forecast API on a 2° grid over the whole region (https://hamarihawa.org/api/wind; dir is where the wind comes from, km/h; step is the grid spacing in degrees), refreshed hourly, drawn as drifting streaks; the Your-air box names the big towns the wind is coming from and heading towards.
- City air: Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo (about 11 km). In winter it reads lower than ground sensors in Lahore and Islamabad by roughly 1.5×.
- Health estimates: cigarettes ≈ PM2.5 ÷ 22 (Berkeley Earth); WHO 24-h guideline 15 µg/m³; life expectancy −0.098 years per µg/m³ above 5 if sustained (AQLI); extra daily deaths +0.68% per 10 µg/m³ above 15 (Liu et al., NEJM 2019). Population-level estimates only.
- Source shares (PM2.5): Lahore, PAQI 2025 (emitted): vehicles 35%, industry 28%, brick kilns 17%, waste 6%. Islamabad–Rawalpindi, PAQI 2025: vehicles 53%, kilns 18%, waste 11%, industry 9%. Punjab (Pakistan), World Bank 2024 (in the air): dust 25%, residential 23%, transport 16%, industry 16%, agriculture 13%, waste 7%. Delhi winter, TERI-ARAI 2018 (in the air): vehicles 28%, dust 17%, industry 16%, biomass 14%, residential 10%, brick kilns 8%, power 6%.

## How people search for this
Often searched in Roman Urdu/Hindi: "Lahore smog aaj", "Lahore ki hawa aaj", "Delhi AQI aaj", "parali ki aag", "parali jalana", "smog kahan se aata hai". Urdu: لاہور اسموگ، پرالی کی آگ. Hindi: दिल्ली AQI आज, पराली जलाना.

## Source code
Open source (code MIT, data licences per file) at https://github.com/hammadtq/hamarihawa
To reproduce the Two Punjabs numbers: scripts/backfill-days.py (needs a free NASA FIRMS key) then scripts/season-stats.py rebuilds site/public/report/two-punjabs/seasons.json.

## Please cite as
HamariHawa (hamarihawa.org), using NASA FIRMS, NASA GIBS / Copernicus Sentinel-5P, Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo, Carbon Mapper, SentinelKilnDB, the Pakistan IGP Brick Kiln Dataset, OpenStreetMap and GeoNames.

## Caveats
- Fire counts since 2021 have fallen by about two-thirds, but the share seen on the 1:30 am pass rose from about 3% (2019) to 8% (2025), consistent with reports of burning moving to late afternoon and evening, between satellite passes. Lower counts may partly be missed fires.
Being shown on this site means satellites detected heat or pollution at a place; it does not identify who lit a fire or show that anyone broke the law.
